newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta steady, traders expect little excitement.
newsitem.headline: Peseta steady, traders expect little excitement.

text.p: The peseta held steady against the mark in subdued morning trade on Monday, and traders said they expected little excitement in the week ahead.
"We are likely to remain in the same narrow range (84.00 - 84.30 to the mark) seen in recent sessions today, and I don't expect any great movements this week," said one trader.
By 1030 GMT, the peseta was at 84.19/22, flat from early levels, and compared with 84.18/19 in late trade on Friday.
Traders said attention on Monday would focus on the European Union finance ministers (ECOFIN) meeting in Brussels and the G-10 central bankers meeting in Basle.
Dollar movements would also be eyed, they added, but with U.S. markets closed for Veteran's Day this was unlikely to stimulate much activity.
Spain's producer price index data did little to nudge the Spanish currency after coming in slightly above expectations.
Spanish producer prices rose 0.3 percent in September and 0.8 percent year-on-year. A Reuters poll had forecast a rise of 0.2 percent on the month.
Traders said they would, however, closely watch consumer price (CPI) data due on Thursday.
"A positive figure will raise expectations that the Bank of Spain will cut interest rates before year-end," said one trader.
A Reuters poll forecast September CPI up 0.2 percent.
Other influences in the week ahead include a series of U.S. data and the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday, they added.
U.S. data due to be released include October producer prices on Wednesday and retail sales and consumer prices on Thursday.
